catalog_quote: I.2.2.5.2.3 Système tonal. Sur le plan tonal, l’opération de commutation a permis de mettre en évidence deux tonèmes, Haut noté / ʹ/ et Bas noté/ ˋ/. Les tons ont une fonction distinctive dans cette langue. Sur le plan syntagmatique, l’auteur notifie que les tonèmes peuvent s’additionner pour donner des tons modulés montant et descendant. De plus, ils peuvent être analysés en schèmes tonals, c’est à dire en succession dans la chaîne parlée. Les schèmes tonals ci-après ont été relevés : Haut-Bas /ngɔ́ndɛ̀/ « lune ». new_statements.translation: Tonally, the commutation test brought out two tonemes, High (marked ´) and Low (marked `). Tones have a distinctive function in this language. Syntagmatically, the author [Mokrani 2016] notes that the tonemes can combine to give rising and falling contour tones. [...] High-Low /ngɔ́ndɛ̀/ 'moon', High-High /kókó/ 'hen', Low-High /tùnʒú/ 'basket', Low-Low /kòlò/ 'foot' [p. 90] ... Synchronically, the data showed that the B20 varieties regularly attest two tonemes (high and low) [p. 218].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sake is described purely as a two-tone (H/L) Bantu language with lexically distinctive tone and HB/HH/BH/BB stem patterns; none of the accessible descriptions mentions word stress or accent placement at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. The only accent-related remark is group-level and diachronic (p. 238): across B20 the stem-final syllable is 'régulièrement réalisée avec un ton bas' and the H/L opposition is fading in stem-final position, which 'pourrai[en]t conforter.. une évolution vers un processus accentuel' (citing Rekanga 2007, Dodo-Bounguendza 2010) — not a synchronic stress rule for Sake.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone patterns given for disyllabic noun stems in isolation (citation forms). The Sake-specific tonal analysis on p. 90 is Koumbi Mabiti's summary of Mokrani (2016); the p. 218 two-toneme statement rests on his own 14-variety data set, which includes Sake informants recorded Feb-Mar 2024.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern Sake/Shake B251 (sake1247). Hombert et al. 1989 and Mamfoumbi 1988/1989 describe the Booué dialect (saké i mèmbónzù, speaker from Djidji near Booué); Koumbi Mabiti's own 2024 Sake data come from young speakers (informant list in his annex), and his phonological sketch of Sake is taken from Mokrani 2016. Jacquot's 1983 'sake' list was also collected around Booué.

sources.note: Sake sketch §I.2.2.5 (pp. 85-90, phonology summarised from Mokrani 2016): two tonemes H and L, distinctive, combine into rising/falling contours; schemes HB, HH, BH, BB (p. 90). Own B20-wide tonal analysis (pp. 215-238): all 14 varieties incl. Sake 'attestent régulièrement deux tonèmes (haut et bas)' (p. 218); notes stem-final syllable regularly Low across the group and speculates on an incipient 'processus accentuel' (p. 238). No statement on word stress placement.
